_doc: RATE-1022: per-portal rate-limit adapters (vera/rate_limit.py). rate_per_s/burst = token bucket; max_concurrency = in-flight cap; daily_cap = requests SENT per UTC day (throttled ones included; skips never sent are not counted). Throttles (throttle_statuses or caller-flagged anti-bot pages) halve the rate (AIMD) and set a cooldown: Retry-After when sent (clamped to retry_after_max_s), else base_cooldown_s doubling per consecutive throttle up to max_cooldown_s, plus upward-only jitter. The breaker opens after breaker_failures consecutive throttles/failures for breaker_open_s (doubling per failed half-open probe, up to breaker_open_max_s). acquire() waits at most min(max_wait_s, caller deadline - min_call_s), otherwise it skips at once. 429/cooldown tries never count as attempts; they are always counted as requests. No email is sent anywhere: contact_param is used only if VERA_CONTACT_EMAIL is set (unset by default).
_calibration_note: UNCALIBRATED against live traffic. Sources were read 2026-10-21 by the research-reader agent through WebFetch (a summarizing fetch, not raw page text: every quote is a paraphrase-level check). Where a portal documents a ceiling, rate_per_s is set at or BELOW it (planner prior chosen for a shared Render egress IP, where other tenants spend the same per-IP allowance); where nothing is documented the value is a planner prior, flagged 'prior'. The AIMD, breaker and cooldown defaults are planner priors (no live spread measured). What would change them: the per-portal 'ratelimit' log line and /health/dar aggregates over a week of live inline runs (429 share, skip share, time in cooldown, and inline yield); raise a rate only up to its documented ceiling.

defaults._note: Planner priors. max_wait_s 2 keeps any in-request wait far below the 45 s inline deadline (config/auto_acquire.json inline.deadline_s); min_call_s 1 is the least time left for a call to be worth sending.

sources.claims: no key 10 req/s, free key 30 req/s; daily budget per key (keyless about a tenth); 429 for daily budget or per-second excess; headers X-RateLimit-Limit/-Remaining/-Credits-Used/-Reset (seconds to midnight UTC)

openalex._note: rate 1.0 = the existing search.openalex.min_interval_s (vera_eval_run.json), max_concurrency 1 = existing; both under the documented 10 req/s. Remaining is a budget unit (credits), so pace=false: only remaining <= 0 sets a cooldown to the reset. base_cooldown_s 900 = the existing search.openalex_quota_cooldown_s (auto_acquire.json), now the no-Retry-After fallback. No mailto (none approved; the page documents none).

sources.claims: no official limit found (observation as of 2026-10-21, not proof of absence); a third-party client defaults to 10 req/s (not official)

europepmc._note: prior. Covers the acquisition search, the resolve_oa DOI search and the fullTextXML (JATS) fetch: one host, one shared budget. max_concurrency 4 = auto_acquire inline.fetch_workers; rate 5/s is half the unofficial 10/s.

sources.inspection: summarizing fetch; Acceptable Use Policy not read

duckduckgo._note: prior. rate 0.2 = existing search.duckduckgo_lite.min_interval_s 5; max_concurrency 1 and daily_cap 8 = existing (vera_eval_run.json). 202 is the anti-bot page seen from Render; the caller also flags challenge-marker pages as throttled. A challenge is never retried or evaded: it starts a cooldown.

arxiv_web._note: prior, ARX-A2 SECURITY-CONFIG CHANGE (needs security review): the arXiv full-text route (vera/arxiv_fulltext.py) reads robots.txt (cached), one abs page and one HTML page per record, one at a time, and itself waits arxiv_route.min_interval_s (or a longer robots.txt crawl-delay, up to arxiv_route.max_crawl_delay_s) between its requests; this portal is the process-wide ceiling: 1 request / 3 s, one connection, no burst. Separate from the export.arxiv.org API portal. What would change it: arxiv.org robots.txt crawl-delay (unverified) and live 429/503 counts.

wikipedia._note: rate 2/s = 120/min, under 200/min, which needs the compliant User-Agent (config/encyclopedia_source.json user_agent carries a project URL, no email). Serial per the etiquette page. base_cooldown_s 5 = the documented no-Retry-After wait.

groq._enabled_note: INT-1022-B (orchestrator disposition 2026-10-22): disabled until calibrated against Groq headers live. /ask makes about 3 Groq calls within a few seconds, which the uncalibrated prior (0.5/s, burst 2, max_wait 1 s) could skip. With enabled=false the OpenAI-SDK clients get no rate-limit transport at all (vera.rate_limit.openai_http_client returns None), so LLM calls behave exactly as at 76ceb2a. Calibrate from live x-ratelimit-* headers and 429 counts, then set true.

sources.claims: 429 with retry-after (seconds); headers x-ratelimit-limit/remaining/reset-requests (per day) and -tokens (per minute), reset as durations such as 2m59.56s / 7.66s; free-tier numbers for the configured model NOT on the public page (account limits page needs login)

groq._note: prior: 0.5/s (30/min) because the free-tier numbers were not readable; the headers then pace the real quota. Covers every OpenAI-SDK client pointed at api.groq.com (provider chain, claim check).

sources.claims: :free models 20 req/min; 50 req/day with under 10 credits purchased (1000/day with 10+); X-RateLimit-* only on 429; Retry-After when providers give a hint

doi_landing._note: P0-5 Step B (config/auto_acquire.json inline.landing_route, ships false): DOI resolver hops and their robots.txt only; no other caller requests these hosts through rate_limit.limited_by_url. Owner-approved publisher hosts (landing_route.publisher_hosts, ships empty) must get their own portal entry, honouring robots crawl-delay, before the flag is enabled.
